title: Saber Denies Using AI to Replace Game Scriptwriters, Former Chief Screenwriter Immediately Retorts: You Can't Have It Both Ways

content_html:
Game developer Saber Interactive is in the midst of a controversy over the credit for the script of its new game, "Rideshare Stimulator." The game, announced last month, was developed by its Unigine studio. Former lead writer Stella Sacco publicly accused the company on social media: "I was the lead writer for this game, but Saber replaced me with ChatGPT during development, and all the passenger voiceovers were also AI-generated." She also questioned whether the official had changed direction midway or intentionally failed to disclose the involvement of AI on the Steam page.

In response to the accusations, Saber CEO Matthew Karch categorically denied them, stating, "Saber and Unigine have not replaced any writers with AI," and added that the game's story was "completely written by humans." He also acknowledged that the game will include an experimental free ride mode, which "necessarily" incorporates AI technology due to the infinite number of passengers. Karch emphasized that since the company's founding in 2001, AI tools have been used to enhance the gaming experience and improve NPC behavior, and he added that none of the company's more than 3,000 employees need to worry about being replaced by AI.

No Disclosure on Steam Page, But AI Traces Are Clearly Visible

The core of the controversy lies in the issue of information disclosure. From the game's trailer, the lines and voices of the simulated passengers clearly show signs of being AI-generated. However, the Steam store page for "Rideshare Stimulator" currently has no statement regarding the use of generative AI. In a time when players' acceptance of AI-generated content is divided, whether to actively disclose the involvement of AI has become an unavoidable integrity test for developers. Hiding such information often causes more outrage than using AI itself.

content_html_zh:
游戏开发商 Sabre Interactive 因其新游戏“Rideshare Stimulator”的剧本归属而陷入争议。 该游戏于上个月宣布，由 Unigine 工作室开发。 前首席编剧Stella Sacco在社交媒体上公开指责该公司：“我是这款游戏的首席编剧，但Sabre在开发过程中用ChatGPT取代了我，所有乘客配音也都是AI生成的。” 她还质疑官方是否中途改变了方向，或者故意没有在Steam页面上披露AI的参与。

针对这些指控，Sabre 首席执行官 Matthew Karch 断然否认，称“Sabre 和 Unigine 没有用人工智能取代任何编剧”，并补充说游戏的故事“完全由人类编写”。 他还承认，游戏将包括一个实验性的免费乘车模式，由于乘客数量无限，该模式“必然”结合了人工智能技术。 卡奇强调，自2001年公司成立以来，人工智能工具一直被用来增强游戏体验和改善NPC行为，他补充说，公司3000多名员工中没有一个人不需要担心被人工智能取代。

Steam页面未披露，但AI痕迹清晰可见

争议的核心在于信息披露问题。 从游戏预告片来看，模拟乘客的台词和声音明显显示出人工智能生成的迹象。 不过，《Rideshare Stimulator》的 Steam 商店页面目前还没有关于使用生成式 AI 的声明。 在玩家对AI生成内容的接受度出现分化的当下，是否主动披露AI的参与已经成为开发者不可避免的诚信考验。 隐藏此类信息通常会比使用人工智能本身引起更多的愤怒。
